parsed.why: The national document, entry-screening and custody exposures remain substantial. State civil-rights protections are enforced and facilities access is not locally restricted, but care and sports limits chiefly affect residents; the incident count lacks a denominator.

The shared national regime remains the principal exposure. State protections and open identity documents offer some mitigation, with a meaningful sanctuary shield in the largest city, but it is geographically limited; sports restrictions remain proposals.

The statewide birth-sex restroom rule creates unavoidable exposure across public facilities, backed by fines and early police ID checks; federal enforcement inquiry and the Do Not Travel assessment reinforce the risk. No documented remedy changes practice.

A criminal restroom ban reaches government buildings and public-facing private businesses, with up to a year in jail. Litigation is unresolved and no enforcement is documented, but the universal, severe exposure compounds the national regime.

The state removed civil-rights remedies and bars localities from restoring them; a school-ground restroom rule also covers visitors. These hostile layers compound national risks, though no general adult facility ban outside schools is documented.
